name: Note
text: Reference tracks that capture the feel you're going for — tempo, energy, instrumentation style. Note WHY each one is a reference, not just that it sounds good.

name: Note
text: Planned instruments/synths per section (intro, verse, chorus, bridge, outro). VST/plugin names and preset notes so a session is reproducible later.

name: Note
text: Section-by-section map: Intro (0:00–0:15) — sparse, filtered pad. Verse (0:15–0:45) — drums + bass enter. Build clear transitions between sections before adding detail.

name: Note
text: Lyric drafts, melody hums/voice-memo references, and theme/story notes if the track has vocals.

name: Note
text: Professionally mixed/mastered tracks in the same genre, used as a loudness and tonal-balance reference during mixing.

name: Note
text:
1. Levels balanced before any processing
2. High-pass non-bass elements
3. Check mix in mono
4. Reference against mix-reference tracks
5. Automate key transitions
6. Leave headroom for mastering (~-6dB peak)

name: Note
text: Target loudness (LUFS) per platform (streaming vs. club vs. broadcast), file format/sample rate required, and metadata (ISRC, credits, artwork) needed for release.
